attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-7
attempts.paper_title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals during active somatosensation
attempts.entry_title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals (Yu et al. 2016)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data. VPM and fast-spiking cells rose with whisking (VPM 4.3 to 11.9 spikes/s), their spikes were phase-locked to whisking, and cutting the infraorbital nerve removed fast-spiking touch and whisking responses. Thalamic photoinhibition lowered fast-spiking rates in direction, but the percentages differed from the paper's. Layer 4 excitatory cells did not show the reported lack of a whisking effect (p about 0.02), and the eNpHR touch-detection findings did not reproduce, although one of them flips with how passive first touches are handled. The inhibition seen at depolarized potentials, the thalamic multiunit photoinhibition and the rabies tracing could not be tested because those recordings are not in the dataset. Several latency and amplitude values were off, and the files do not say which tracked whisker is the principal one.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Gutnisky, Hires and Svoboda (2016) on CRCNS ssc-7, which holds spikes and membrane potential of VPM units, L4 excitatory neurons and L4 fast-spiking interneurons in mice localizing a pole with their whiskers, with whisker tracking, touch annotations, licks and optogenetic trials. It compares baseline, whisking and touch responses of the three cell types, the effects of infraorbital nerve transection, thalamic photoinhibition and PV interneuron suppression. The thalamic multiunit recordings, the rabies tracing and the recordings with depolarizing current injection are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yu et al. (2016) from CRCNS ssc-7

outcomes.notes: Under every combination of readings only cortical performance is within tolerance (0.706 over all good trials, 0.721 over control trials, n = 111 cells). VPM performance is 0.630 (n = 29). Touches per trial are 7.56 (Go, 7,097 trials) and 1.06 (Nogo, 6,872 trials) over the whole trial, 2.74 and 0.36 before the first lick. The reaction time is 328 to 340 ms. Proximal touches outnumber distal ones under every reading. With the principal whisker taken from the whisker configuration (variant), Go 5.93 and Nogo 0.63.
deviations: Touches are counted on the first tracked whisker series, taken as the principal whisker (an assumption; the files do not say which series is the principal whisker, see findings). The configuration-order reading is shown as a variant.

Proximal and distal trials are read as Go and Nogo trials (Online Methods, Behavior, "licked ... if the pole was in one of the posterior locations"). Trial counts pool the cortical recordings and each VPM session once; the paper's 4,147 and 4,173 trials cannot be matched to a set.
The data set's good-trial masks are applied.

outcomes.notes: The nonwhisking mean is 4.34 to 4.82 spikes/s under the four readings (within 5.1 +- 1.02), the median 1.99 to 2.18 (outside 3.3 +- 0.33). Range 0.03 to 17.66 spikes/s. Seven units from one mouse (ANM199552) have a mean of 9.78.
deviations: Epoch rules follow M-EPOCH; whisking cycles run from one phase wrap to the next, and the margin readings (a) and (b) of the claims file are both shown.

outcomes.notes: Spikes per touch 0.50 +- 0.43 (median 0.363, within tolerance; the mean is just outside). The latency is 2.48 ms on average and 1 ms median (n = 25 passing the exclusion; 13 units cross in the first 1 ms bin). Read at the bin centre, 2.98 ms (within) and median 1.5 ms (outside). The duration is 4.08 ms. The population PSTH peaks 2 ms after touch onset. The 1 ms difference in the median latency is not explained; the trial-type columns are Hit, Miss, CR, FA in the VPM files as in the cortical ones.

The first touch of trials tagged passive touch is left out, as the data set's example code compute_touchNWB.m does; its touch-speed cutoff is not applied.

outcomes.notes: Under M-SIG reading (b), per-trial rates, 24 increase, 1 decreases and 4 do not change, with either nonwhisking margin. Under reading (a), per-epoch rates, 22 or 21 increase and 6 or 7 do not change, outside tolerance. Whether the unchanged units respond to touch was not tested. The readings give different outcomes; the criterion accepts a match under one reading.

outcomes.notes: Nonwhisking 4.34 +- 4.79 and whisking 11.92 +- 11.67 spikes/s, ratio 2.74, signed-rank p = 5.2e-8, n = 29; all four sub-readings within tolerance. The onset variant gives 4.61 to 9.92 spikes/s (p = 3.7e-9).

r2 > 0.25 in 27 of 29 units with 8 phase bins and 25 of 29 with 16. Coupling strength median 1.63 spikes/s (0.13 to 6.54), preferred phase median -0.38 rad. With spikes shuffled across whisking samples, 14 of 29 still pass the r2 cutoff, so the cutoff is weak.

All 37 amplitudes are positive. The latency median (5.0 ms) and the amplitude median (5.4 mV) are within tolerance. The latency mean (6.03 ms, n = 35) and the amplitude mean (5.26 mV) are not. Medians 0.87 mV (whisking) and 5.42 mV (touch); the signed-rank test gives p = 2.9e-11 under every reading. With the per-trial threshold line of M-VM, the touch mean (5.74 removed, 5.81 kept) is within tolerance and the whisking mean (-0.236 +- 5.89) is not. The largest whisking shift, -28.9 mV (JY0947), comes from a line through two thresholds in trials 126 and 129. The principal-whisker variant gives p = 6.1e-6.

Where every threshold of a neuron falls in one trial, the per-trial line is not defined, and their mean is used; the first run fitted a line there. outcomes.notes: Per neuron (n = 35), the touch reversal (median -49.8 mV) exceeds the whisking reversal (median -58.7), p = 2.6e-5, and lies above resting Vm in 34 of 35. The median whisking reversal is 4.9 mV above the median resting Vm (-63.4), inside the 5 mV margin, but close to it. Pooled, touch -45.4 and whisking -57.6 mV. One touch fit had a non-negative slope and was left out.

outcomes.notes: Over 36 neurons, whisking power exceeds nonwhisking power, 10 to 100 Hz (median ratio 1.17, p = 0.046), and 10 to 500 Hz (1.18, p = 0.030). 24 and 30 neurons have whisking power above the nonwhisking 95% bound over most of the band. The 10 to 100 Hz p is close to 0.05.

outcomes.notes: The six neurons recorded at rest and depolarized near 0 mV by current injection (Fig. 3) are not in the data set. Every ephys trial of every whole-cell file was read (the counts match the whisker trials). No L4 E trial has a median Vm above -42.8 mV and no L4 E current exceeds 0.2 nA, JY0978 (the cell list's Fig. 3 example) included. The only trials near 0 mV are the first 18 of the FS neuron JY1139, which keeps firing (8 to 85 spikes per trial) with no current above 0.1 nA, a drifting recording, not the protocol; JY1171 carries a steady current above 0.5 nA at -40.7 mV. No part of the claim can be tested.
Needs the depolarized recordings of Fig. 3, which are not in the data set (see l4e-inhibition-window); no part can be tested.
The 26 FS neurons of the two control FS folders give 9.43 +- 8.33 spikes/s, median 6.3; all four readings within tolerance.

The seven whole-cell FS neurons give an amplitude of 6.8 +- 1.93 mV (median 6.97) and a latency of 3.67 +- 1.18 ms (median 3.9). outcomes.notes: The claim of no whisking effect fails its test. The signed-rank test of whisking against nonwhisking rates gives p = 0.020 to 0.027 under all readings (mean difference 0.29 to 0.33 spikes/s, median 0). Spikes per touch are 0.20 (median 0.04) against 0.3 (0.1). The nonwhisking mean and the whisking median are within tolerance under every reading; the nonwhisking median is within under rate reading (a) (0.092) and outside under reading (b) (0.116 to 0.121). Whole-cell neurons give 0.096 spikes per touch, cell-attached ones 0.28. The 17 thalamic multiunit recordings with patch pipettes during TRN-axon photostimulation are not in the data set; the only thalamic recordings are the 29 silicon-probe units, which have no photostimulation. The bucket listing and every member of data.tar.gz were checked.

In the light period, Vm outside touch is lower in all 13 neurons (median -2.99 mV, p = 0.00024), and the 10 Hz high-passed variance falls to 0.59 of control (p = 0.00024). The rule as written crosses at the onset sample (0.0 ms), where dVm/dt is -295 and -392 mV/s. With 1 ms smoothing and a 1 ms hold, the thalamic latency is 4.8 ms (13 neurons) and the cortical one 2.6 ms (8 neurons). The thalamic latency is longer, and the cortical one is within tolerance. Over smoothing windows of 0.5 to 2 ms and holds of 0.5 to 2 ms, the thalamic latency is 4.5 to 5.0 ms and the cortical 2.0 to 2.7 ms; the thalamic one is always longer and no window puts both within tolerance.
deviations: The latency rule is read with 1 ms smoothing and a 1 ms hold, so that the step the light makes at the onset sample is not taken as the response. This is an assumption; the rule as written gives 0 ms for both.
Direct cortical activation trials are those with only the vS1 473 nm series on, in VGAT-ChR2 mice (8 neurons with an average; the paper has 7).
13 neurons, where the paper has 12.

outcomes.notes: Per-trial Spearman correlations between light power (control 0) and rate inside the light period are negative for nonwhisking (12 of 13, p = 0.00049), whisking (13 of 14, p = 0.0012) and touch (12 of 14, p = 0.0012). Ten neurons have two powers (3.8 and 15 mW), four have one. The test as fixed mostly compares light with no light. Among light trials only, in the neurons with two powers, median rho is -0.58 (nonwhisking, 6 neurons, p = 0.31), -0.28 (whisking, 10, p = 0.074) and -0.23 (touch, 7, p = 0.031): one epoch of three. A question on the criterion is asked of a reader.
deviations: The correlation is taken over trials of each neuron, not over per-power means, which with two or three power levels give only two or three points. The multiunit variant was not run, as those recordings are not in the data set.

0.492 correct pooled over 1,335 trials of 19 ION-cut cells in 7 mice; the mean over cells is 0.510. The mice still whisk (median per-trial amplitude 1.60 degrees, against 2.56 in controls).

The measure (peak minus baseline) is positive by construction. At random times it gives 0.208 mV, and touch does not differ from that (p = 0.148). The controls give 5.26 mV. With the onset measure and the 17 controls whose resting Vm lies within the ION-cut range (reading a), 0.582 +- 0.35 against 1.337 +- 0.98 mV, rank-sum p = 0.033. The ION-cut mean is within tolerance; the control mean lies 0.003 mV below the bound of 1.34. 0.061 +- 0.115 spikes per touch (median 0.040, n = 10), signed-rank against zero p = 0.098; the controls give 1.83.

The paper shows no data for these neurons ("data not shown"), and the ION-cut folders hold only L4 neurons (the cell list gives depths of 444 to 614 um for the ION-cut FS neurons).

Four groups within the light period, H = 18.0, p = 0.00044 (n = 43); two groups p = 0.00022. Whole trials, p = 0.021. The cell list names 43 L4 E neurons from PV-IRES-Cre mice; the 43 here are those less JY0781 (no eNpHR light in its file) plus JY1268, which the cell list does not name. The paper's 40 cannot be matched to a subset.

outcomes.notes: Within the light period, nonwhisking 0.54 +- 0.11 to 1.45 +- 0.31 (p = 0.00012) and whisking 1.13 +- 0.24 to 2.82 +- 0.54 (p = 3e-5). Both tests hold; three of four means are within tolerance (the control whisking mean is not). Over whole trials the rises are smaller.
In eNpHR trials, whisking 2.82 against nonwhisking 1.45 spikes/s, p = 0.013 (light period), or p = 0.0065 over whole trials. In control trials, p = 0.052 (light period) and 0.035 (whole trials).

Both means are within tolerance, but the mean change is significant (signed-rank p = 0.009; 0.027 over whole trials), and the correlation between control response and change is not (rho = -0.13, p = 0.42; whole trials -0.22, p = 0.16). One of the three parts holds.

With the first touch of trials tagged passive left out, Spearman rho = -0.23, p = 0.16 (M-ROC reading a) and rho = -0.28, p = 0.09 (reading b), n = 37; the rank-sum variant gives p = 0.1 and 0.43. With those passive first touches kept, as in the first run, rho = -0.34, p = 0.038 under reading (b), so the outcome rests on the choice (143 trials tagged passive). Regression to the mean is small here: with control trials split in halves, the evoked rate of one half does not correlate with the AUC difference between halves (rho = 0.02, p = 0.91), and with rate and control AUC from different halves the claim's correlation is rho = -0.19, p = 0.27. Under reading (a) with the passive first touches kept, rho = -0.29, p = 0.086. Six neurons lack enough touch or no-touch trials. A question on the criterion is asked of a reader.
deviations: The AUC is computed over whole trials (the first touch, or a reference time, with 250 ms windows), as M-ROC describes; the light period is not applied.

The first touch of a trial tagged passive is not the trial's first touch; a trial whose only touch is that one is left out. An assumption: M-ROC says "the first touch", and the paper studies active touch, and the data set's compute_touchNWB.m leaves passive first touches out, as touch_table does for every other claim.

outcomes.notes: The AUC rose in 17 and fell in 20 neurons (reading a), or 24 and 13 (reading b). With raw rates and reading (a), the increased-AUC group's touch-evoked rate goes from 2.04 to 3.16 spikes/s (p = 0.04) and the reduced-AUC baseline rise (3.53 to 4.20) is not significant (p = 0.083); under reading (b) the increase is not significant (p = 0.069 to 0.084). At most one of six rates is within tolerance under any combination.

Three of four PV neurons are strongly inhibited in the light period (rates at 0.05, 0.21 and 0.09 of control, rank-sum p < 1e-9); the fourth is unchanged (1.08, p = 0.64). On the sparse grand-average PSTH (1 ms bins), neither latency rule finds the PV decrease. The L4 E increase crosses at 17 ms (dPSTH/dt) or 7 ms (rate).
deviations: Strong inhibition is judged inside each trial's light period, by the criterion's rank-sum test and halving.

outcomes.notes: In the recording sessions of the 9 mice with eNpHR trials, 4 show a significant decrease in Nogo performance with light and none an increase, against 6 of 8 and 1. Leaving out any one mouse gives 3 or 4, so no 8 of the 9 match. No session matches the example (closest JY1247, false alarms 14% to 58%). Light falls in 23% to 48% of Nogo trials here, where the example describes "a small subset of trials". Per session the light share of Nogo trials is 14% to 70% (median 37%; 3 of 47 sessions under 20%). One mouse (ANM266951) has 7 Nogo trials and cannot give a significant result; without it, 8 mice give 4 decreases.
deviations: Tested on the recording sessions, assumed to be the sessions of Supplementary Fig. 14. The paper does not say which sessions it used, and the data set holds no other behavior with eNpHR light. Against the assumption: 9 mice here against 8, and no session matches the example. For it: the mouse with 7 Nogo trials may be the one the paper does not count, and some sessions have light in a small share of Nogo trials.

findings.statement: In the cortical files the whisker timestamps (processing/whisker/BehavioralTimeSeries/*/timestamps, labelled Seconds) are the trial start in milliseconds plus the time within the trial in seconds, so trial starts are 1,000 times those of the ephys timestamps. Read as milliseconds, each ephys trial starts 10 ms before the first whisker frame (10 kHz files) or with it (20 kHz files).

Seventy cortical files hold two tracked whisker series (whisker_angle_1, whisker_angle_2, with their touch annotations), and nothing says which whisker each is. Mapping them in the order of general/whisker_configuration to analysis/principal_whisker gives FS neurons almost no touch response (0.45 against 1.78 spikes per touch with series 1), while for several L4 E neurons it picks the series with the larger touch response (JY1345 0.857 against 0.235). The example code takes the first whisker as the main one.

Not in the data set, though the paper reports them. The 17 thalamic multiunit recordings during TRN-axon photostimulation (Fig. 6b,c), the rabies tracing (Supplementary Fig. 10), the L5 FS neurons after ION cut, and the whole-cell recordings with depolarizing current injection (Fig. 3, n = 6). No whole-cell L4 E trial has a median Vm above -42.8 mV.

The neuron JY1139 in the L4FS_whole_cell folder has the unit description "Excitatory", while the folder and the cell list's FS sheet give it as an FS neuron. Its first 18 trials have median Vm between -2.3 and -26.8 mV while it fires 8 to 85 spikes per trial with no injected current above 0.1 nA; from trial 20 it sits near -41 mV. Nothing in the file marks these trials.

Eight whole-cell L4 E files (JY0865, JY0861, JY1002, JY0989, JY0913, JY1009, JY0781, JY0986) flag 132 stimulus trials in analysis/trial_type_mat but hold no photostimulus series, and Exp_2015-09-24_004 and JY1633 have 23 flagged trials without light in their series. What stimulus these trials had cannot be read.

The eNpHR experiments hold 43 L4 E neurons with 594 nm light trials (39 cell-attached and 4 whole-cell), where the paper gives 40. Thalamic photoinhibition has 13 whole-cell L4 E neurons against 12, direct cortical activation 8 against 7, and the mice with eNpHR light number 9, where Supplementary Fig. 14 has 8.

For the authors. The onset latency of Vm after light onset (Supplementary Fig. 9c,f; 4.2 and 2.8 ms) is not defined in the paper. The touch rule (dVm/dt crossing 3 s.d. of its baseline) crosses at the onset sample, where the light makes a step in the average Vm. How was the light artifact handled, and was dVm/dt smoothed?

For the authors. Which tracked whisker series is the principal whisker in the files with two series, and was the touch-speed cutoff of compute_touchNWB.m (prct_speed 2.5) applied in the paper's analyses? Was the first touch of a trial tagged passive used as the trial's first touch in the ROC analysis of Fig. 8f,g? The correlation of enphr-auc is significant with it (p = 0.038) and not without it (p = 0.09).

The cell list (docs/yu_gutnisky_CellList.xlsx, sheet AllCellsReported) does not name JY1268, which the cell-attached L4 E folder holds with eNpHR light trials; its "Extracellular units" section has 47 rows against 48 files. It lists JY0781 among the PV-IRES-Cre L4 E neurons, though that file holds no photostimulus series.

entries.name: crcns-ssc-7-yu-2016
entries.title: Layer 4 fast-spiking interneurons filter thalamocortical signals (Yu et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Gutnisky, Hires and Svoboda (2016) on CRCNS ssc-7, which holds spikes and membrane potential of VPM units, L4 excitatory neurons and L4 fast-spiking interneurons in mice localizing a pole with their whiskers, with whisker tracking, touch annotations, licks and optogenetic trials. It compares baseline, whisking and touch responses of the three cell types, the effects of infraorbital nerve transection, thalamic photoinhibition and PV interneuron suppression. The thalamic multiunit recordings, the rabies tracing and the recordings with depolarizing current injection are not in the data set.
